people.name: Becky Ball
people.bio: Professor in the School of Mathematical and Natural Sciences at Arizona State University since 2010; before that she held a postdoctoral position in environmental studies at Dartmouth College (2007-2010).

people.name: Kelli Larson
people.bio: Human-environment geographer who joined Arizona State University in 2005 and is a professor in its School of Geographical Sciences and Urban Planning and School of Sustainability. Lead social scientist for the CAP LTER, director of the Phoenix Area Social Survey, and founding director of ASU's SURE undergraduate research program.
people.research_interests: Human-environment geography; urban and landscape sustainability; environmental planning and management; public perceptions, attitudes and behaviors; residential gardening and human-wildlife interactions

people.name: Stevan Earl
people.bio: Data manager at Arizona State University (Knowledge Enterprise) since 2015.

people.name: Quincy Stewart
people.bio: Site manager for the Central Arizona-Phoenix LTER at Arizona State University since 2020.

people.name: Nancy Emery
people.bio: Evolutionary ecologist and professor at the University of Colorado Boulder; as lead principal investigator of the Niwot Ridge LTER she oversees the project, its staff, budget and annual NSF reporting. Her lab studies how plants adapt to and persist in variable, changing environments.
people.research_interests: Evolution of dispersal; habitat specialization; phenotypic plasticity in plants of variable environments; population, community and evolutionary ecology

people.name: Sarah Elmendorf
people.bio: Information manager and quantitative ecologist for the Niwot Ridge LTER, overseeing data archiving and quality control and analysing long-term, multi-site data on climate-change impacts, especially phenology and alpine tundra plant communities.
people.research_interests: Phenology; tundra plant community ecology; ecological impacts of climate change; long-term and multi-site data analysis

people.name: Eve-Lyn Hinckley
people.bio: Interdisciplinary environmental scientist (biogeochemistry and hydrology) and associate professor at the University of Colorado Boulder; Niwot Ridge LTER co-PI who co-leads biogeochemical measurements and advises on long-term surface-water sampling. Studies how human activity alters flows of carbon, nutrients and water.
people.research_interests: Human alteration of carbon, nitrogen, sulfur and mercury cycles; water and nutrient fluxes; use-inspired biogeochemistry

people.name: Will Wieder
people.bio: Ecosystem modeler and soil biogeochemist: research scientist at the University of Colorado Boulder and project scientist at the National Center for Atmospheric Research. Co-PI of the Niwot Ridge LTER, leading its integration and modeling work and bringing ecological insight into Earth system models.
people.research_interests: Soil biochemistry; Earth system modeling; tropical forest ecology; global biogeochemical cycles

people.name: Jennifer Morse
people.bio: Lead field technician and staff scientist for the Niwot Ridge LTER; runs collection of the site's climate and hydrology data, telemetry for its meteorological stations and sensor networks, and field logistics with the CU Mountain Research Station.

people.name: Lauren Hostert
people.bio: Field science manager at the National Ecological Observatory Network since 2022. Earlier a stream ecologist (assistant scientist) with the Illinois Natural History Survey, University of Illinois (2018-2022), and a senior field ecologist in NEON's Domain 11 field operations (2014-2018).

people.name: Amy Jacobs
people.bio: Manages NEON field operations in the Great Basin (D15) and Northern Rockies (D12) domains from Salt Lake City. Earlier career in oceanographic research on marine bacterioplankton and in leading coastal habitat restoration for the State of Florida; master's degree in biology (University of West Florida).

people.name: Scott Taylor
people.bio: Evolutionary biologist and ornithologist; professor at the University of Colorado Boulder and director of its Mountain Research Station. As a Niwot Ridge LTER co-PI he leads the long-term chickadee breeding study; his group uses hybrid zones to study the genetics of speciation.
people.research_interests: Hybrid zones and speciation; genetic basis of reproductive isolation; effects of climate change on species distributions and interactions

people.name: Jason Williams
people.bio: USDA-ARS hydrologist: Research Leader and supervisory research hydrologist at the Northwest Watershed Research Center since 2024, after serving as a research hydrologist at the ARS Southwest Watershed Research Center (2016-2024) and, from 2006 to 2016, as a hydrologist at the Northwest Watershed Research Center.

people.name: Frederick (Fred) Pierson
people.bio: USDA-ARS scientist, now an associate director of the ARS Pacific West Area, who previously spent 17 years as Research Leader of the Northwest Watershed Research Center. Known for rangeland ecohydrology research on juniper encroachment and fire effects on runoff and erosion, and for helping build the RHEM erosion model.
people.research_interests: Rangeland ecohydrology; fire effects on runoff and soil erosion; woodland (juniper) encroachment; rangeland conservation practices; Rangeland Hydrology and Erosion Model (RHEM)

people.name: Kathleen A. Lohse
people.bio: Ecosystem scientist and professor at Idaho State University working where ecology, earth-system science and hydrology meet; director of the NSF Reynolds Creek Critical Zone Observatory since 2013, and now senior personnel or collaborator in the CZ Network geomicrobiology and drylands clusters.
people.research_interests: Ecosystem responses to human-driven change; critical zone science; biogeochemistry and hydrology
